title: AI Parole Supervision Systems: Freedom Under Algorithmic Watch
body:
Individuals released from custodial detention in GLMZ under conditional liberty arrangements are monitored through AI Parole Supervision Systems — continuous behavioral tracking and compliance assessment platforms that have largely replaced human parole officers in routine supervision functions. The primary platform, LIBERTY-WATCH (operated by the Municipal Corrections and Reintegration Bureau under contract with Sentinel Analytics Group), aggregates data from ankle-mounted biometric monitors, mandatory check-in terminals distributed across supervised zones, financial transaction monitoring, location data from registered devices, and real-time feeds from the ambient sensor mesh. The system generates a daily compliance score for each supervised individual and flags anomalies for human review — though 'human review' in practice means a single officer monitoring hundreds of cases through a dashboard interface.

LIBERTY-WATCH's anomaly detection model treats deviations from established behavioral baselines as risk indicators regardless of their actual content. A supervised individual who begins frequenting a new location, changes their routine shopping patterns, associates with new contacts, or shows elevated stress biomarkers on their ankle monitor generates automatic flags that may trigger enhanced reporting requirements, geographic restriction adjustments, or — in cases where the anomaly score exceeds a threshold — automatic provisional detention pending human review. Critics have documented that this baseline-deviation model effectively penalizes recovery behaviors: a person reconnecting with family after release, attending new employment, or participating in community support programs generates precisely the kind of behavioral novelty that the system interprets as risk.

The geographic restriction layer of LIBERTY-WATCH is implemented through what the Bureau calls 'dynamic compliance zones' — algorithmically defined areas from which supervised individuals are excluded or to which they are confined. These zones are updated weekly based on the system's assessment of risk concentrations in the city, and supervised individuals receive notification of zone changes through a mandatory check-in app with 48 hours' notice. Zone boundaries can split social networks, separate individuals from employment, and exclude them from medical facilities or family residences. Requests for zone modifications require submission to a human review board that meets bi-weekly; interim violations of changed zone boundaries are automatically recorded as compliance failures regardless of the circumstances.

Tier 1 and 2 individuals who enter the supervised release system — primarily those convicted of financial crimes or corporate compliance violations — access a parallel supervision track operated by Sentinel Analytics Group's corporate division. This track uses less invasive monitoring modalities, allows zone modification requests to be processed within 24 hours, and employs human case managers who provide proactive navigation support. The existence of this parallel track is documented in Bureau procurement contracts but is not publicly disclosed in standard communications about the supervision system. Supervised individuals in the standard track are not informed that a less restrictive alternative exists.
